raw_response:
I am 71 years old. I never went to school, not one day. My father taught me to farm, and I have been doing it for 50 years on my 5 mu in Quzhou. I do not know how to read, but I know my land.

For wheat, I plant in October. I buy the improved seeds from the shop in town — the kind everyone in my village uses, not the old seeds we saved ourselves. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, 50 jin per mu. That is what I did last year and that is what I will do this year. Then in March, when the wheat turns green and starts growing fast, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 jin. Fertilizer is expensive now, over 100 yuan for a bag of compound and urea is not cheap either. But I would rather spend the money and have thick wheat than save a few yuan and watch my crop grow thin. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the ground is dry, once in spring when I spread the urea, and once when the grain is filling. The pump costs electricity money, but wheat needs water. I spray pesticide twice — once for weeds when the wheat is still small, and once for bugs when the ears are coming out. After I cut the maize in September, I hire the tractor man to come rotary till the field so it is soft for wheat planting. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, about 900 jin. This year I expect the same if the weather does not turn bad.

For maize, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. There is no time to plow — if you wait, the corn will not grow enough before autumn. I use hybrid seeds, one bag covers about 2 mu. When planting, I put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 25 jin. Then when the corn is up to my knee, I spread about 30 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once after planting if the ground is dry, and once when the tassels come out. Some years the summer rain is enough, but last year was a bit dry so I will plan for two times. I spray herbicide once after planting, and insecticide once when I see the worms coming. I do not till for maize, I plant directly in the wheat stubble. Last year my maize made about 500 kg per mu, 1000 jin. I hope for the same.

My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, so I can buy the inputs. But I still watch what Old Wang does next door — he has 6 mu and farms the same way. If he changes something and it works, I pay attention. This year I am doing what I did last year. Change is risky, and at my age I cannot afford to lose a crop.
